title: The 2,000-Year-Old Computer #Shorts

hook.narration: In nineteen oh one, divers pulled a two-thousand-year-old computer from the sea.

visuals.prompt: A corroded bronze gear mechanism glowing faintly underwater among ancient shipwreck debris

scenes.narration: Sponge divers exploring a shipwreck near the Greek island of Antikythera found a corroded lump of bronze.

visuals.prompt: Early twentieth century sponge divers in heavy brass helmets descending beside a wooden boat off a rocky Greek island
A diver's hand lifting a green corroded lump of bronze from the seabed

scenes.narration: Inside were dozens of precisely cut gears.

visuals.prompt: Macro shot of tiny ancient bronze gears with fine triangular teeth, green patina, museum light

scenes.narration: Researchers later worked out that it modelled the movements of the sun and moon, and predicted eclipses.

visuals.prompt: An ancient Greek astronomer turning a bronze dial beside a model of the sun and moon, warm lamplight
A total solar eclipse over an ancient Greek coastline

scenes.narration: Nothing this complex is known again for over a thousand years.

description: The Antikythera Mechanism is an ancient Greek device that tracked the heavens with gears. Here is how it was found. #Shorts #History #AncientGreece

thumbnail.prompt: Bronze gears of an ancient mechanism glowing against dark water, mysterious
